method.value: Calculate flare light curves at ALMA Band 3 and VLA Band X using the van der Laan (1966) expanding plasma blob model. Estimate lower limit on companion mass transfer rate by requiring free-free absorption optical depth tau_ff >= 1 at 1.25 GHz.

analysis_steps.goal: Simultaneous MCMC modelling of high-mode and low-mode broadband SEDs

method.value: De-redden NIR/optical/UV fluxes, construct mode-resolved SEDs from radio to X-rays, and perform simultaneous MCMC sampling of the high-mode model (irradiated star + multi-colour disc + compact jet broken power law + shock synchrotron) and low-mode model (irradiated star + multi-colour disc + compact jet broken power law + discrete ejecta optically thin power law).

evidence.quote: To perform the fit to the SED, we used a model comprising a blackbody of an irradiated star and a multi-colour accretion disc, together with a broken power law to describe the optically thick and thin components of the synchrotron emission from the compact jet. In addition, we considered a power law to model the optically thin emission from the discrete ejecta at all frequencies.

In particular, we considered that the X-rays are produced by the sum of the optically thin component of the synchrotron emission from the base of the compact jet and the synchrotron emission from the region of shock between the pulsar wind and the inner flow.

Employing both datasets (high and low mode), we performed an MCMC sampling of the posterior probability density function for the parameter space of the two models simultaneously (since some of the free parameters are shared by both models).
The NIR, optical and UV data obtained on Night 2 were de-reddened assuming $A_V=0.17\pm 0.01$ mag

analysis_steps.goal: Fit the millimetre-X-ray luminosity correlation for black hole XRBs and compare with J1023

method.value: Perform Bayesian MCMC linear regression on log L_mm vs log L_X for black hole XRBs (including upper limits) using LINMIX_ERR with 10^4 posterior draws.

claims.hypothesis: Switches from the X-ray high mode to the low mode in PSR J1023+0038 are triggered by discrete mass ejections that remove the inner accretion flow and shock region, while a compact jet persists across both modes.
claims.experiment: Conducted simultaneous multi-wavelength observations across two nights (including ALMA Band 3, NICER, XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, HST, Swift, VLT, REM, NTT, VLA, FAST), extracted mode-resolved light curves and SEDs, searched for short millimetre flares, and modelled the high- and low-mode SEDs and flare properties.
claims.result: Detected two brief (~15 s) millimetre flares up to 1.01 +/- 0.08 mJy (one occurring at a high-to-low mode switch), found average mm flux densities of 89 +/- 13 uJy (high mode) and 134 +/- 23 uJy (low mode), measured shorter X-ray low-mode ingress (10.4 +/- 6.9 s) than egress (30.6 +/- 8.2 s) times, and successfully fit both mode SEDs (Bayesian p-values 0.78 and 0.07) and flare properties with a van der Laan expanding blob model.
claims.finding: The high-to-low mode switch is connected to short millimetre flares that mark discrete mass ejections removing the inner flow and shock emission, while an underlying compact jet and expanding discrete ejecta account for the low-mode multi-wavelength emission.

evidence.quote: The first episode (hereafter ‘Flare 1’) occurred on 2021 June 26 within the time range 22:19:29 – 22:19:44 (UTC) at the switch from high mode to low mode and reached a peak flux density of 1.01$\pm$0.08 mJy.

During the high mode, synchrotron radiation at the shock front between the pulsar wind and the inner accretion flow produces most of the X-ray emission, as well as X-ray, UV, and optical pulsations. The switch to low mode is triggered by discrete mass ejections, resulting in a drop in the X-ray flux and a quenching of pulsations.

claims.hypothesis: Radio pulsations from the rotation-powered pulsar in J1023 are absent during the active sub-luminous X-ray disc state due to free-free absorption by enshrouding matter transferred from the companion star.
claims.experiment: Searched 3 hr of FAST 1.25 GHz observations covering 21 low-mode episodes and inferior conjunction for folded, periodic, single-pulse, and saturated radio signals, and calculated the mass transfer rate required for free-free optical depth tau_ff >= 1.
claims.result: No radio pulsations were detected down to 5sigma upper limits of 2.0 +/- 0.5 uJy (total), 2.2 +/- 0.6 uJy (high mode), and 4.7 +/- 1.0 uJy (low mode), implying a companion mass transfer rate >= 10^-11 M_sun yr^-1 for tau_ff >= 1.
claims.finding: No pulsed radio emission is present in either mode down to the most stringent limits to date, which is explained by free-free absorption from enshrouding material if the mass transfer rate is >= 10^-11 M_sun yr^-1, implying most transferred mass is ejected.

evidence.quote: and derived a 5-$\sigma$ flux density upper limit for persistent radio pulsations of 2.0$\pm$0.5 $\mu$Jy at 1.25 GHz considering the entire integration time of 2.8 hr

claims.experiment: Compiled quasi-simultaneous 100 GHz millimetre and 1–10 keV X-ray luminosities for black hole and neutron star XRBs, fit the black hole L_mm - L_X correlation using LINMIX_ERR, and compared J1023's mode-resolved luminosities to the relation.
claims.result: The black hole L_mm - L_X relation has a slope beta = 0.46 +/- 0.09, and J1023's low-mode luminosities (L_mm = (3.0 +/- 0.5) x 10^28 erg s^-1, L_X = (3.6 +/- 0.4) x 10^32 erg s^-1) lie within the 3sigma region of this correlation.

why_this_data.value: Simultaneous multi-wavelength coverage from radio and millimetre through NIR, optical, UV, and X-rays is required to connect X-ray mode switching to jet/ejection phenomena and model the broadband SEDs in the high and low modes.

evidence.quote: This paper presents the results of the largest multi-wavelength campaign ever performed on J1023. Our aim is to ultimately understand the root cause of the mode changes in the active sub-luminous X-ray state and its implication for our understanding of the accretion-ejection coupling in XRB systems that harbour rapidly spinning NSs.

why_this_method.value: Simultaneous MCMC fitting of both high- and low-mode SEDs allows sharing common physical parameters across modes while using wide uniform priors to avoid excluding true source parameters; time-resolved ALMA imaging on scan, mode, and 15 s timescales probes both minute-scale variability and rapid flares.

evidence.quote: The integration times adopted above are effective for studying the variability of the millimetre emission on minute timescales, but may average out large enhancements of the millimetre flux on much shorter timescales (of the order of seconds). Therefore, we performed a dedicated search for short flaring episodes by extracting images of different durations using the entire dataset.

Employing both datasets (high and low mode), we performed an MCMC sampling of the posterior probability density function for the parameter space of the two models simultaneously (since some of the free parameters are shared by both models).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Intrinsic magnetospheric phenomena (intermittency or nulling) as the cause of the non-detection of radio pulsations, rejected because such phenomena were never observed when J1023 was in the radio pulsar state.

evidence.quote: The non-detection of radio pulsations could be due to ‘intrinsic’ phenomena within the pulsar magnetosphere (i.e. irrespective of the presence of external drivers such as accreting material) such as intermittency and/or nulling (see e.g. (cite: weng22) for recent similar considerations for the system LS I $+$61 303). However, these phenomena were not observed during extensive radio timing campaigns when the system was in the radio pulsar state (e.g. (cite: archibald13; stappers14)), so they are unlikely to be the cause of the non-detection.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Scattering of radiation on the accretion disc surface as the origin of the optical linear polarisation, rejected due to the lack of modulation of the Stokes parameters with the binary orbital period.

evidence.loc: Optical polarisation measurements and predictions of X-ray polarisation
evidence.quote: Given the lack of modulation of the Stokes parameters with the orbital period, it is unlikely that the source of the polarisation is scattering of radiation in any region of the system (such as the surface of the accretion disc), in contrast to previous suggestions (cite: baglio16).

limitations_admitted.value: No flare was observed simultaneously at two different frequencies (ALMA and VLA were on different nights), preventing proper constraint of the van der Laan expanding blob model parameters.

evidence.loc: Millimetre flares as the fingerprint of discrete ejecta
evidence.quote: Since no flare in this study was observed simultaneously at two different frequencies, we are unable to properly constrain the model parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: Scarce low-frequency data points and overlapping IR/optical components cause strong parameter correlations in the SED fit (between nu_sync and F_sync, and between F_0 and alpha_1).

evidence.quote: This is however not surprising considering the scarce number of points at the lowest frequencies and the impossibility to constrain quantities such as $\nu_{\rm break}$ and $\nu_{\rm sync}$, due to numerous overlapping components at infrared and optical frequencies.

limitations_admitted.value: Significance of optical linear polarisation in high and low modes separately is not high enough to distinguish between a jet origin and a shock origin (compatible within 1sigma).

evidence.loc: Optical polarisation measurements and predictions of X-ray polarisation
evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the significance of our polarisation results obtained in the high and low modes separately is not high enough to verify this, as the results are compatible with each other within $1\sigma$ ($0.36^{+0.27}_{-0.35}\%$ in the low mode and 0.65$\pm$0.43% in the high mode).

referee_caveats_inferred: VLA (Night 1) and ALMA (Night 2) observations were not simultaneous, so combining radio and millimetre flux densities in the mode-resolved SEDs relies on the assumption that the average radio flux in each mode is stationary across weeks.

Only two out of seven high-to-low mode switches covered by ALMA showed detectable millimetre flares, meaning the link between every mode switch and a discrete millimetre flare relies on invoking variable ejecta properties or absorption.

Table 4 (Tab:fit_res) in the paper text is missing the printed posterior median values for the shared parameters (T_*, Log r_in,opt/UV, Log nu_break, alpha_1, alpha_2, Log F_0), although some are quoted in the text and shown in Figure 11.
